description: Two-panel composite figure on the corrosion behaviour of low-density steels (LDSs) in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. (a) Potentiodynamic polarization curves: semi-logarithmic plot with current density (A/cm²) on a logarithmic x-axis spanning 10⁻⁸ to 10⁻¹ and potential (V_SCE) on the y-axis from −1.5 to 0.0. The legend lists four samples — S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta) — drawn with distinct symbols. The cathodic branches of all four curves nearly overlap, converging near −0.9 V_SCE; the anodic branches then show a small current peak around −0.6 V_SCE before flattening into a low-current plateau near −0.45 V_SCE that extends to ≈10⁻² A/cm². (b) Scatter plot of breakdown current density i_bre (µA/cm²) versus sample, y-axis 0-15, with error bars; printed mean values are 9.92 (S0), 2.72 (S950), 6.55 (S1050) and 8.84 (S1150). Together the panels show that the fine-grained S950 sample has the lowest breakdown current density and therefore the best corrosion resistance, whereas the untreated S0 is most prone to corrosion.

observations.observation: Panel (a) has current density (A/cm²) on a logarithmic x-axis from 10⁻⁸ to 10⁻¹ and potential (V_SCE) on the y-axis from −1.5 to 0.0.
Panel (a) legend lists four samples: S0 (red), S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta), each plotted with a different symbol.

In panel (a) the four cathodic branches nearly overlap, while the anodic branches separate and show a small current peak near −0.6 V_SCE before levelling into a plateau at roughly 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴ A/cm² near −0.45 V_SCE.
Panel (b) prints four breakdown current density values in µA/cm²: 9.92 for S0, 2.72 for S950, 6.55 for S1050 and 8.84 for S1150.
Panel (b) has error bars on all four points of the i_bre values.
The caption states that (a) shows potentiodynamic polarization curves and (b) the corresponding breakdown current density of LDSs in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.

The citing text states the cathodic polarization curves of all samples nearly overlap and primarily involve the oxygen absorption reaction, so the grain-size change from solution treatment has negligible influence on the cathodic reaction.

The citing text divides the anodic process into three regions: active dissolution from −0.91 to −0.67 V_SCE, a decreasing unstable region from −0.67 to −0.58 V_SCE indicating surface oxide film formation, and a subsequent near-constant current region attributed to a protective oxide film / passive-like behaviour.
The citing text states that S0 without solution treatment has the highest i_bre (9.92 µA/cm²) and is relatively more prone to corrosion.
The citing text states the fine-grained S950 sample has i_bre = 2.72 µA/cm², lower than the coarse-grained S1150 at 8.84 µA/cm², giving S950 higher corrosion resistance.
The citing text states that the error bars in panel (b) represent the standard deviation of the tests and that error values of all samples are controlled within 5 %, indicating good repeatability.
The citing text states that a lower breakdown current density indicates better corrosion resistance.

subfigures.description: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for S0, S950, S1050 and S1150 in 3.5 wt% NaCl; current density (A/cm²) on a log x-axis 10⁻⁸ to 10⁻¹, potential (V_SCE) on the y-axis −1.5 to 0.0. Cathodic branches overlap almost completely; anodic branches display a peak near −0.6 V_SCE followed by a passive-like current plateau near −0.45 V_SCE.

Point plot of breakdown current density i_bre (µA/cm², y-axis 0-15) against the samples S0, S950, S1050, S1150, with error bars. Printed values: 9.92 (red star), 2.72 (green circle), 6.55 (blue triangle), 8.84 (magenta symbol).
